items.rationale: Flour combines with water or milk in dough. The explanation describes mixing/kneading; it does not imply that all dough varieties have identical ingredients.

Fresh egg pasta is made from flour and eggs, then rolled and cut. These are coherent alternative entries to one general pasta concept.

Beaten eggs and sugar form the aerated base for sponge cake, with flour incorporation and baking explicitly required by the explanation.
Bread is baked dough; the explanation specifies bread dough and acknowledges leavening variation. The pair is a conceptual baking transformation.
Milk coagulation by rennet and draining whey is a real cheese-making route. Both the producer ingredient list and a worked home recipe support it.
Lemon juice coagulates heated milk; the explanation correctly describes an acid-set fresh cheese rather than claiming this is every cheese-making process.
Dissolving salt in water produces brine. This is a direct transformation; the game gives no preservation quantities or safety instructions.
Cornmeal is boiled and stirred in water to make mamaliga; heating is explicitly stated in the explanation.
Mamaliga may be cooked in milk or milk mixed with water. The text says this is a variant and does not replace the classic water route.
Telemea is a salted cheese stored in brine. The explanation treats salting/storage as the distinguishing transformation, not arbitrary milk-to-product taxonomy.
Bulz combines mamaliga and cheese; telemea is an attested option. The explanation names filling and baking instead of claiming any unheated serving is bulz.

Fruit cooked with sugar is a conventional preserve route. The explanation acknowledges fruit-dependent proportions and does not promise a complete preserving procedure.
Apple pieces can be cooked with sugar to make apple preserve; this is a legitimate specific-fruit route to the same general preserve concept.
Compot is prepared from fruit and water, generally sweetened. The explanation explicitly includes optional sweetening and cooking.
Apples are a conventional compot fruit, cooked in water with sweetening to taste; the general result label is accurate.
Vegetables including cucumbers are fermented in brine to make pickles. A producer explicitly describes natural brine fermentation; the explanation claims no instant real-world pickling.

Vegetables cooked in water form a vegetable soup base. This broad result matches the broad ingredient class.
Fermented bran bors is a souring ingredient for ciorba. The text describes a real souring route without claiming all ciorbe require bors.
Boiled beans are central to bean ciorba and bors is an attested optional souring ingredient. The shortcut explanation names the additional vegetables and boiling.

Crushed garlic is central to mujdei; water thins it and oil can emulsify a creamy variant. Salt/crushing and the variant distinction are stated.

Cooked mashed beans flavored with garlic form the basis of fasole batuta. The explanation names cooking and mashing, not raw-bean mixing.
Rice-and-vegetable stuffed peppers are an attested fasting variant. The explanation clearly identifies the omitted vegetables.
Peppers stuffed with minced meat and rice are conventional; the explanation names both rice and seasoning beyond the selected pair.
Roasting prepared meat in an oven produces friptura. The broad result does not invent a specific cut or named regional dish.
Tomato and cucumber are a conventional fresh vegetable salad base. The broad result label avoids claiming a distinctive regional recipe.
Fresh cheese can be served or mixed with sour cream. This is a literal serving combination, acceptable outside a hidden-target challenge.
Unfermented cream suitable for whipping is aerated with a mixer into whipped cream. The source ingredient is specifically whipping cream, not generic sour cream.
Vanilla custard contains milk, vanilla, egg and/or starch with sugar. Both explanations name necessary omitted thickening ingredients; these are conceptual base-ingredient recipes.

Romanian home chocolate is made with cocoa and milk powder plus sugar syrup and butter. This is a documented home variant, not a claim about all industrial chocolate.
Flour and butter are characteristic short biscuit ingredients; sugar and baking are named in the explanation. It is not presented as a complete two-ingredient cooking recipe.
Broken biscuits and cocoa/chocolate are characteristic components of biscuit salami. A chocolate variant is directly documented by its recipe author.

Dough layers around apple filling are a straightforward apple-pie association; no unsupported regional-origin claim is added.

Walnut and cocoa fillings occur in cozonac. The explanations specifically require sweet leavened dough; generic dough alone is not claimed to be sufficient. Predictability among pastries is the separate quality review.

Fresh cheese and flour are characteristic papanasi dough components, with egg explicitly acknowledged as another ingredient.
Boiled papanasi can be made with fresh cheese, semolina and egg. The explanation accurately limits the route to the boiled variant.
Semolina-and-egg dumplings are cooked in soup. The omitted egg is explicit, preventing the false implication that loose semolina alone forms dumplings.
Cremsnit consists of baked pastry sheets with vanilla cream; the explanation explicitly identifies puff pastry as the required dough subtype.
Poale-n brau are folded leavened pastries with sweet cheese. The explanation names the dough subtype and folding. Specificity against other cheese pastries remains a quality concern.
Sweetened whipped-cream bases are used for frozen home ice cream. The explanation says a suitable sweetened base can become ice cream, not that plain frozen cream is identical.
A vanilla custard base may be chilled and frozen for ice cream; the explanation correctly qualifies the cream as suitable rather than treating every pastry custard identically.

Sour cabbage leaves wrap a minced-meat-and-rice filling in conventional Romanian sarmale. Rice and seasoning are explicitly acknowledged.
Fasting sarmale can use rice and vegetables in sour cabbage leaves; the meat-free route is factual rather than an invented substitution.
Frying portions of leavened dough in oil produces a familiar doughnut variant. Leavening and sweetening are named, not assumed to result from oil alone.

world_rationale: All 57 exact recipes and their explanations were independently checked against live dictionary, author-recipe, educational or producer evidence. These are explicitly simplified culinary idea pairs, not complete cooking instructions; necessary omitted processing or ingredients are acknowledged. Four inherited concept descriptions were corrected locally to cover meat-free stuffed dishes, ordinary flour pasta and non-season-specific compot, while retaining KG snapshots and provenance. No recipe claims regional exclusivity or changes with a selected goal. Common pantry concepts and recognizable dishes meet the broad Romanian-relevance baseline; recipe specificity and long-term play quality remain the separate independent quality judgment. No claim is made that every possible pair works.
